title: Dealing with an embedded ball in a penalty area
question: Your ball is plugged in the ground inside a penalty area. What are your options according to the rules?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies.
Take relief under the penalty area rule for a penalty stroke.
Repair the ground before you play your shot.
Move the ball outside the penalty area without penalty.
Take a penalty stroke and play another ball from where you last played.

explanation: You can play the embedded ball as it lies, or take penalty relief under the penalty area rule by dropping outside for one penalty stroke, or take stroke-and-distance relief by playing a new ball from the original spot for a penalty stroke. Free embedded ball relief is not allowed in a penalty area.

juniorVersion.title: What can you do if your ball is stuck in the ground in a penalty area?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball has landed in a penalty area, like a pond or a muddy place, and is stuck in the ground (plugged). What can you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it is, without touching it first.
Take a penalty and drop a ball, following penalty area rules.
Fix the ground before you hit your shot.
Move the ball out of the penalty area without a penalty.
Take a penalty and hit a new ball from where you last hit.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball is stuck in the ground in a penalty area, you can play it as it is, or you can take a penalty and drop or play a new ball. You are not allowed to fix the ground or move the ball out for free.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A special place on the course, like a lake, pond, or very muddy ground, where different rules apply.
A ball that is stuck in the ground so you see only part or none of it above the surface.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show what it looks like when a ball is plugged in soft ground. Practise what you can do inside and outside a penalty area.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you always get to fix the ground when your ball is plugged.
Thinking you can always move the ball with no penalty when it is stuck.
Thinking a plugged ball can always be dropped for free from a penalty area.
